meta.model: Brown & Batygin 2021 reference population (CaltechDATA v3), 100,000 samples
meta.exclusions: Published binary detectability flags for ZTF (Brown & Batygin 2022), DES (Belyakov et al. 2022), PS1 (Brown et al. 2024), applied exactly as published
meta.propagation: Two-body Kepler from published elements + geocentric correction; validated in docs/validation.md (epoch reproduction limited by published element precision: median ~53 arcsec; 8.4-yr drift vs JPL n-body <= ~111 arcsec on Sedna-class orbits)
meta.candidates: Published infrared candidate positions (unconfirmed); see per-marker notes
meta.mpc_distant_census_note: Count of MPC distant objects meeting the SCT26 census filters (90<a<1000 AU, q>30 AU, U<7) as of build date. Objects without a published 4-Gyr stability classification cannot be added to the clustering sample; see docs/method.md.

candidates.name: IRAS F02211-4844 (1983)
candidates.note: IRAS position of the single IRAS-AKARI candidate pair; source absent at this position in AKARI 23 years later. Authors state two survey positions do not determine an orbit; follow-up required. One AKARI band flux may be unreliable.

candidates.name: AKARI-MUSL J0220440-491247 (2006/07)
candidates.note: AKARI position of the same candidate pair, ~40 arcmin from the IRAS position 23 years earlier (consistent with orbital motion at several hundred AU, per the authors). Unconfirmed; follow-up required.

candidates.name: FISSSDL J0250422-150114
candidates.note: Detected twice within 24 hours, not re-detected after six months. Fluxes vary between detections; physical properties unconstrained. Unconfirmed; could be a transient event.

candidates.name: FISSSDL J0301112-164240
candidates.note: Same selection as the other AKARI candidate. The paper could not pair any candidates via expected Planet Nine parallax. Unconfirmed.
